title: Four short paragraphs that say what the resume cannot
takeaway: Hook, one proof with a number, the gap named plainly, a short close: specific, honest, and every claim checkable.
sources: A cover letter is only worth writing when it can say something the resume structurally cannot.
Specific, honest about the gap, and every claim is checkable.

data.heading: New graduate letter, under 200 words
lines: I have been using [Product] since my second year of university,
and the thing that made me apply was the changelog entry about rebuilding the diff view.
The most relevant thing I have built is a self-hosted analytics tool that ingests and aggregates about two million events a day.
I have not worked full-time as an engineer yet. What I do have is eleven merged pull requests to [open source project].
Happy to talk any time. Code and resume attached.

notes.note: The hook: why this company, concretely, and unfakeable at scale
Proof: one relevant thing built, with a number
The gap named in one sentence, then the mitigation
